content.text:
**Finding: compliant (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

Investigation summary:
- **p0493 (§12.2(d))** — the only competing-product mechanic. It is a *RevMed termination right* triggered if Sanofi develops/manufactures/commercialises a Competing Product, with a cure/election window and a carve-out where Sanofi has already commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product. It contains no "shall not" operator: Sanofi remains free to pursue a Competing Product. That belongs to the termination checklist, not NONCOMPETE.
- **p0500–p0505 (§12.3(c))** — consequences are the ordinary licence-reversion/grant-back package on termination, not a penalty covenant.
- **p0037 (§1.20 "Competing Product")** — definitional only (largely redacted); no operative prohibition attaches to it.
- **p0612–p0614 (§15.2)** — the firewall/separation duties (separate R&D activities, no Know-How exchange) apply "In the case of RevMed" as a condition to excluding acquiror IP; Sanofi's counterpart at p0612 carries no such conditions, so nothing binds our side.
- **Article XIII** — §13.3 covenants run against RevMed only; §13.4 mutual covenants cover debarment, compliance and pharmacovigilance. No competing-activity or territory covenant on Sanofi.
- **Field** is defined as "any and all uses", so there is no field-of-use restriction on the licence either.

Noted for the file (rationale only, not a deviation): §12.2(d)'s "Competing Product" scope is redacted, so if the redacted criteria prove broader than expected we would revisit it under the termination rule rather than here.
